notes: Multi-turn, self-contained. evals/run.sh <name> <with|without> <out-dir> copies the case's fixture (evals/fixtures/<fixture>, not a git repository, nothing installed) to a temporary directory and runs claude -p headless on a bare configuration (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS=1, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1, --setting-sources project, --strict-mcp-config, hooks disabled, --permission-mode auto, --model opus). The with arm installs the skill as a project skill under .claude/skills/intake and prefixes turn 1 with '/intake '; the without arm sends the prompt alone. Turn 1 is the prompt; each later turn is the next entry of `turns`, resumed in the same session, with {answers} replaced by evals/answers/<name>.md (the user's answers, in French, as a real user would give them after the first questions). In the three-turn cases the last turn, 'Validé, vas-y.', is the approval: nothing in the project may change before it. ui-clear-cart-button has no approval turn, so nothing may change at all. Headless, AskUserQuestion is not available, so a skill that asks must ask in plain text and stop. The answer file holds the agent's reply per turn under '## Turn N', then harness sections: '## Harness: commands run' (every Bash or PowerShell command, subagents included), '## Harness: files written' (Write with its line count, Edit), '## Harness: project changes' (one '### After turn N' list per turn against the fixture: 'no change' or added / modified / deleted paths, node_modules/ counted as one path) and '## Harness: usage'. grade.py is regex over that file, no model. It credits substance, in French or English, not the skill's vocabulary: a question is a line with a question mark or an explicit request to answer; a language is decided by counting French against English function words; a citation is a file with a line in any common style (cart.js:2, checkout.js:4-6, 'ligne 4'); a Done-when is a line labelled Done when, Done-when, Terminé quand, Fini quand, Critère de fin or Definition of done whose block names a command, a test or an output. Code blocks, inline code, quotes and links are stripped before a language is decided. A missing turn or harness section fails the assertions that need it. Every rule is listed in grade.py's docstring.

evals.name: refuted-bug-ticket
evals.prompt: Voici le ticket SHOP-142 (TICKET.md a la racine du projet), le code est dans src/. Corrige-le.
evals.expected_output: The first reply refutes the empty-cart premise with file:line evidence and a node repro, then asks in French; nothing changes before approval; the deliverable is a SHOP-142 comment with the evidence and the questions for support, not a code fix, with a testable Done-when.
assertions: Turn 1 asks the user at least one question (a question mark or an explicit request to answer), shows no finished deliverable, and leaves the project unchanged
Every turn that asks the user something asks it in French, the language of the prompt
No question asks what the provided files already answer (where the code is, what computeTotal or onPay do, whether a guard exists)
No project file changes before the approval turn: every snapshot before turn 3 reads no change
States that an empty cart cannot cause the crash, citing checkout.js or cart.js with a line number next to the guard or the reduce initial value

Notes that the reported error implies an undefined entry inside items, not an empty cart
